#1748. Attacking efficiency key for Hull’s visit

Arsenal are in Premier League action this afternoon, taking on Hull City at home. No doubt there will be some rotation from the midweek Champions League game, with players like Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes, Myles-Lewis-Skelly, Jurrien Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Christos Tzolis and Kai Havertz all potential inclusions. I suspect Declan Rice will start!

I wrote yesterday about Viktor Gyokeres and whether his good performance in midweek would see him keep his place. On the Swedish international, Mikel Arteta said:

I think everybody was so happy to see, not only the goals but also the performance, how free he looked, how happy he looked, the energy that he could transmit on that football pitch. That’s exactly what we need, that’s what we’re signing, that’s the type of player that can help us to make the difference and he certainly did that during the night.

So let’s see if that means he keeps his place up front. Noni Madueke has had a decent couple of weeks too, with the manager revealing he’d used the elongated Interlull in October to up the ante in terms of his own training:

What he did is he went abroad and he trained. He got somebody to train him and he went into a programme, he wanted to do that. That’s Noni and that’s his mindset – he wants to get better. I love that action that he took because at that moment he wasn’t playing.

With Bukayo Saka injured and Max Dowman suspended until after the Newcastle game, he’s more or less the only option on the right-hand side, so fingers crossed he can continue that form today against a team who are likely to try and make life difficult for us. Players who can beat a man and find some space are really valuable for fixtures like this, and he might prove very important later on.

Hull started the season brightly, but haven’t won since the end of August. All the same, five draws from their last seven games tells you they’re a relatively tough nut to crack, and with a back five they’ll surely have looked at how other teams have come to our place to frustrate us. An early goal is always useful, Ezri Konsa’s quick strike against Everton probably prevented that game from being as much of a slog as it might have been, but we might also need some patience today too.

Some of the difficult games they’ve come through and competed in, they’ve earned the right to be here and been impressive. We’ve been discussing that with the boys on what to expect from them tomorrow and to be clear on what we need to do to beat them.

Arsenal were a bit wasteful in midweek against Slavia Prague, and so making the most of our chances will be important today. Whether it’s Gyokeres or Havertz, and regardless of the construction of the midfield, we need to be more clinical as a team in general, so let’s hope we can produce that today. I take nothing for granted in this league, but hopefully this is one we can just deal with as efficiently as possible before we head into the Interlull.

I just want to mention the launch of The 22 we had at Big Red last night, a huge thanks to everyone who came along and bought a book. The reaction to it was fantastic, and it was real pleasure to meet so many of you. A massive thanks too to Martin and Louise and all the staff there who were such a great help – with the Tollington closed for a while, Big Red is open today if you’re looking for your pre-game pints.

The last batch of books will go on general sale today at 6pm (UK time) via this link (which will be live at that time): https://www.yumastudios.com/store/p/the-22

Orders are limited to two per person, and once they sell out, that’s it. This is a real collector’s item, and the best of luck if you’re after one.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. Don’t forget the updated Arseblog apps also have a cool new matchday centre, full of stats, alerts, and much more.

Hopefully catch some of you a bit later on!

#1747. Napoli vs Lazio - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 15:25, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 15:29

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Sparking crisis talks between the coaching staff and club president Aurelio Di Laurentiis, Napoli are in danger of missing this season's objectives with several months left to play.

On Wednesday night, the Partenopei suffered a chastening 4-1 defeat to Porto, meaning they have lost seven of their last eight Champions League away games. Having finished 30th in the 36-team table last term, they currently sit 27th - inside the elimination zone.

A former finalist with Juventus, head coach Massimiliano Allegri has personally lost nine of his last 11 matches at Europe's elite level, and he is also under pressure for some dire domestic results.

Napoli lie eighth in Serie A after last week's 2-0 defeat to Juve, and with a 14-point deficit to surprise leaders Lazio they are surely out of the title race.

Defeat this weekend would result in their worst start since 2007, and Allegri cannot expect any favours from his former midfield general at AC Milan.

While Gennaro Gattuso has lost all five of their meetings in management, recent events suggest that trend could soon end.

Including a frantic 3-3 draw in the Derby del Sole, Napoli have gone six games without a clean sheet while conceding 13 goals, and they must now host Roma's fierce city rivals.

Precedent is certainly on Lazio's side, having won on all of their last four visits to Naples and prevailed in five of the last eight meetings overall.

More pertinently, the capital club have just won six consecutive Serie A games, leaving their more optimistic fans dreaming of a first Scudetto since the 1999-2000 campaign.

Gattuso will not be drawn on such talk, even though his side boast the division's joint-best defensive record and have scored at least twice in their last eight matches.

This century, only four teams have previously hit 28 points after 10 matchdays, and that tally has lifted them three clear of reigning champions Inter Milan.

Along the way, Lazio have also had 12 different goalscorers, with Gustav Isaksen finding the net four times in his last five appearances.

The Danish winger was on target in last week's 2-1 win over Cagliari, as the Biancocelesti capitalised on Inter's Milan derby defeat and took sole possession of top spot.

Now, Gattuso will return to a club where he won the Coppa Italia but was subsequently sacked, seeking an incredible sixth straight away win in Serie A.

Adding to the sense of crisis in Naples, Allegri has been hampered by a long injury list for several weeks.

Alessandro Buongiorno, David Neres, Costantino Favasuli, Alisson Santos, Leonardo Spinazzola, Benoit Badiashile and Stanislav Lobotka are all unavailable, while two full-backs are facing a race against time.

Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Mathias Olivera both sustained muscular injuries last weekend, when Luca Marianucci was sent off against Juventus and incurred a one-match ban.

Despite his advancing years and chequered fitness history, Kevin De Bruyne may be asked to go again, having scored three goals in his last five league games.

Without Europe to consider, Gattuso has made relatively few changes so far, and it should be a settled Lazio side that takes to the field on Sunday.

However, he will have to replace captain Mattia Zaccagni, who could be ruled out until next month with a thigh strain.

Albert Gudmundsson is still sidelined after dislocating his shoulder on Iceland duty, but with Adam Marusic and Nicolo Rovella finally back in full training, everyone else should be available.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Vergara; Giovane, Hojlund

Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Sutalo, Provstgaard, Tavares; Frattesi, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

#1746. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb

INS:Johan Manzambi ⇠ Freiburg, £50mJoao Gomes ⇠ Wolves, £34mAlejandro Garnacho ⇠ Chelsea, LoanModou Keba Cisse ⇠ LASK, £5m

OUTS:Youri Tielemans ⇢ Manchester United, £36mDonyell Malen ⇢ Roma, £20mMorgan Rogers ⇢ Chelsea, £117mLewis Dobbin ⇢ Southampton, £10mEnzo Barrenechea ⇢ Benfica, £10

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

“It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. To achieve that; to win the Bundesliga, the cup and the Champions League, we need the whole squad to be fit and healthy. We need to make good use of them and improve the squad. We have already done that, but hopefully it will help us achieve our goals.”

Your Aston Villa team to face Bayern Munich in Hong Kong 👊 pic.twitter.com/VxyopTRMFp

special, one-off lettering and numbering for our clash with Bayern Munich in Hong Kong ✨ pic.twitter.com/7v3cEk5vec

July 21- Walsall 0 Aston Villa 5July 25- Porto 2 Aston Villa 1July 28- Aston Villa 2 Real Sociedad 4August 1- Indonesia All Stars 1 Aston Villa 3August 4- BG Pathum 1 Aston Villa 3Today- Aston Villa vs Bayern MunichAugust 12- PSG vs Aston Villa (Uefa Super Cup)August 15- Borussia Monchengladbach vs Aston Villa

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1745. GdS: Predicted XIs for Milan vs. Ferencvaros – Amorim opts for young line-up

AC Milan welcome Ferencvaros to San Siro this evening, hoping to begin righting the course after a difficult start to their Europa League campaign.

Defeats to Benfica and Bournemouth – both without scoring – in the opening three rounds have left Milan languishing down in 24th in the table. That means they need to be almost perfect to maintain any hopes of a top eight spot, with five games left to salvage things.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

They face a Ferencvaros side who are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and have won all three of their games in Europe so far, so they will arrive in Milan full of confidence and ready to try secure a historic result.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport has the team news ahead of tonight’s game, starting with the absentees. Mike Maignan is suspended, while Strahinja Pavlovic, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Pietro Terracciano and Samuel Chukwueze are all out.

The back four should consist of Filippo Terracciano, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Davide Bartesaghi ahead of the young goalkeeper Lorenzo Torriano, who will step up in Maignan’s absence.

Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse should operate in wide roles either side of a double pivot composed of Yunus Musah and Ardon Jashari. Adrien Rabiot is expected to play a more advanced role behind striker Goncalo Ramos.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos.

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Comotto, Modric, Moreira, Pulisic, Camarda.

#1744. FC Twente vs Ajax - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 06 Nov 2026 16:02

The standout fixture of gameweek 12 in the 2026-27 Eredivisie campaign sees FC Twente and Ajax face off at De Grolsch Veste.

Both teams begin Sunday’s heavyweight clash inside the top four, with the possibility that one could finish the weekend at the summit.

Just four days after recording their biggest-ever league win away at SBV Excelsior in a 9-0 thrashing, Twente faced a more demanding continental test against Pafos on Thursday, coming from behind to claim a 3-1 victory in their third Conference League outing.

One of three teams still boasting a perfect record in Europe’s third-tier competition, Trots van het Oosten are in pole position to reach the knockout stages of a UEFA tournament for the first time since 2011, continuing to make waves in their first full season under John van den Brom.

Riding their joint-longest winning run in over three years, Twente now face arguably their toughest test of the campaign so far. Emerging unscathed would only intensify the growing whispers of a potential title challenge.

The Tukkers have beaten this weekend’s opponent just once in the last five meetings, though that victory came in the most recent clash back in April, when Ramiz Zerrouki and Bart van Rooy netted to seal a 2-1 win.

With only 10 goals conceded - the fewest in the division - a newfound defensive solidity has underpinned Twente’s success so far. It also helps that they have been quick starters, scoring first in eight of their last nine league outings.

Ajax were also in Conference League action in midweek, running riot against Danish side Midtjylland with a 6-1 thrashing at the MCH Arena, picking up where they left off in their last league outing against AZ Alkmaar.

That marked a fifth consecutive victory, as Michel’s men have wasted no time in bouncing back from a three-match winless run either side of the September/October international break - a spell that threatened to derail their ambitions for the season.

Currently the only Eredivisie side with a perfect away record, De Godenzonen now head to Enschede aiming to stay within touching distance of leaders Feyenoord, who could be five points clear by the time proceedings get underway in Twente.

Up against the league’s top scorer, Wout Weghorst, and the leading assist provider, Sondre Orjasaeter, Ajax have their work cut out in their quest for consecutive victories at De Grolsch Veste for the first time since 2021.

Like their hosts, Sunday’s visitors have delivered the first blow more often than not lately - breaking the deadlock in each of their last five outings - and will hope it continues in a fixture whose last six editions have seen them concede the opener five times.

Stav Lemkin (muscle) has yet to feature for Twente this season and is ruled out on Sunday, alongside fellow defender Max Bruns.

First-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall remains sidelined, so Joel Drommel should make a ninth consecutive start between the sticks.

Twenty-year-old Filip Thorvaldsen has endured an injury-hit debut campaign and is once again out of contention for the hosts.

Ajax are contending with a lengthy injury list, with up to eight players potentially missing this weekend’s clash.

Caio Henrique and Anton Gaaei are significant absentees at the back, while the loss of Sofyan Amrabat and Julian Brandt further limits Ajax’s midfield options.

Viktor Tsygankov, Simon Adingra, Kasper Dolberg, and Oliver Valaker Edvardsen remain unavailable in attack, meaning leading scorer Tolu Arokodare is unlikely to be rested after his brace against Midtjylland.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst

Ter Stegen; Wijndal, Janse, Bouwman, Rosa; Baas, Mokio; Gloukh, Klaassen, Ouazane; Arokodare

Given the strong form of both sides, Sunday’s clash could go either way and is difficult to call.

As a result, we are leaning towards a share of the spoils, with honours even at the full-time whistle.

#1743. Jude Bellingham's Dad scores SEVEN for England's OVER-50s side on same day superstar son nets for Real Madrid

Published: 06:17 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:18 EDT, 3 November 2026

Jude Bellingham's father Mark scored seven goals as he represented an England veterans side in a match against the Republic of Ireland.

Bellingham played up front for England Veterans' Over 50s side in a 13-1 victory on Sunday.

The 50-year-old struck six times in the first half of the match and provided an assist to give England a 7-0 lead at the break.

Bellingham added his seventh of the match in the second half as the England side cruised to victory.

Mark's goalscoring feat came on the same day that superstar son Jude scored in Real Madrid's 3-0 victory over Racing de Santander in LaLiga.

The Bellingham family were denied a unique hat-trick over the weekend, with Jobe having seen a goal ruled out as Borussia Dortmund were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich on Saturday.

Mark Bellingham, circled, scored seven goals for England Veterans' Over 50's team against the Republic of Ireland on Sunday. Source: Facebook/EVFC

The father of Real Madrid superstar Jude, 23, and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe, Mark played for the England Veterans' Over 50's side for the first time (Source: judebellingham/Instagram)

The Bellingham family came close to a unique hat-trick at the weekend as Jude scored for Real Madrid, but Jobe had a goal disallowed as Borussia Dortmund lost to Bayern Munich

A talented non-league striker in his heyday, Mark Bellingham netted over 700 goals across at least 20 different clubs, including Leamington, Stourbridge and Sutton Coldfield Town.

He even earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career, which ended in 2017.

Mark made his first appearance for England Veterans Over 50s side, who were crowned Seniors World Cup champions this year, clinching their ninth title in Thailand.

When not playing football of his own, Bellingham is regularly seen attending his two sons' matches.

A Southend United supporter, Mark introduced Jude to football, with the England star's first live matches coming alongside his father at Roots Hall.

Speaking about his father in a recent interview, Jude said: 'We talk about footballing heroes, and my dad was like my first.

'When you go and watch him play every week in non-league, you know it's not the Premier League or anything, but seeing the way that he played and the atmosphere, it made me fall in love with football so he was probably my first hero.

'After the first few times of going, I'd start to pay a bit more attention to the games and stuff, the atmosphere and he's scoring goals so you see him celebrating and stuff like that - you want that to be me.

'Growing up, he'd always give me tips on what I could do and now it gets to a certain age and it sort of flips and that's brilliant because we have that sort of relationship like father and son and then as I got older, like coach and player.'

Mark helped set up Stourbridge Juniors, Jude’s first club, and was a sergeant before fully focusing on his sons’ careers.

He became their agent and negotiated Jude’s £88.5million transfer to Real Madrid from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, and dealt with Dortmund again when Jobe moved there from Sunderland in 2025.

A former West Midlands Police officer, Bellingham earned the nickname the 'Non-League Pele' during his 25-year career. Pictured above with Jude (Source: CJPhillips1982/X)

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup together this past summer

While in Germany, Mark reportedly held an emotional discussion with Dortmund sporting director Sebastian Kehl after being left unhappy by Jobe's substitution at half-time during his Bundesliga debut.

German publication BILD added at the time that Mark sought a meeting with manager Niko Kovac directly – and 'made no secret of his opinion'. The club proceeded to ban all family members from the dressing room following the incident.

Mark’s influence as an agent is said to have stretched to Jude’s media duties when with England. Notably, the player has gone out of his way to speak more at this most recent World Cup, but at previous tournaments he had avoided speaking beyond his obligations despite his increasing influence within the squad.

Mark and Jude and Jobe's mother, Denise, are understood to have separated but remain close, the pair having attended Jude's games at the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico this past summer.

#1742. Man United transfer news: Michael Carrick faces 'exciting' £23m battle with Chelsea and Arsenal for midfielder

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 16:14

Manchester United will have to battle the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea for Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, the latest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are readying themselves for their final game before the start of the November international break, with the club set to welcome Aston Villa to Old Trafford on Sunday.

A defeat could leave the team in the Premier League's relegation zone, and that would almost certainly lead to the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

United's struggles this campaign can in part be explained by the fact their midfield has performed poorly all season, including newcomer Carlos Baleba, who is now set for a period on the sidelines due to a hamstring injury.

It should come as no surprise to see the club linked to more midfielders, though TEAMtalk report that if United are to sign Galatasaray's Batrakov, they may have to convince the Russian to join them ahead of Arsenal and Chelsea.

Valued by Transfermarkt at just over £23m, Batrakov is unlikely to command a significant fee given he has never played in any of Europe's top five leagues.

The midfielder has performed excellently for Galatasaray, scoring five goals while providing three assists in 12 games for the club this season.

Four of those goals came in the Champions League, with the 21-year-old netting twice against Stuttgart, once against Lille and once against Barcelona.

Batrakov can play as either a number eight or an attacking midfielder, though he is arguably at his best when allowed to charge into the penalty area, so perhaps he could be seen as a replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

However, asking him to come to England and step into the void that could be left by the club's captain would be risky, and he should not be relied upon as a starter.

United should not be in a position where they need to sign yet another midfielder after signing three last summer.

It is alarming that co-owners INEOS, who reportedly have control over sporting decisions at Old Trafford, are seemingly admitting that their midfield revamp was a failure.

The Red Devils will also need to rebuild their defence over the next two transfer windows, while there are concerns about the level of their attack, so it remains to be seen if United will be able to fill the holes in their squad.

#1741. Fonseca revisits bitter Milan exit: “I didn’t even get a phone call”

Paulo Fonseca has strongly hinted at being unhappy with how his experience at AC Milan came to such a sudden end.

Fonseca joined Milan ahead of the 2024-25 season, tasked with replacing Stefano Pioli who had won a Scudetto and reached a Champions League semi-final. However, he did not even last until the end of the year before being sacked after a draw with Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It wasn’t a very well-kept secret that the Portuguese was under pressure, and it didn’t take long until Sergio Conceicao replaced him in what seemed to be a manoeuvre orchestrated mainly by agent Jorge Mendes.

Fast-forwarding to the past week, Fonseca abruptly left Lyon in order to return to Portugal with Sporting CP, with whom he signed a contract until 30 June 2030. He takes the place of Rui Borges, and during the press conference (via Calciomercato.com) he revealed some details.

“I think there was a phone call. It happened around the time the rumours started circulating that Rui had refused to speak to me.

“Yesterday I had the pleasure of speaking with him: it was a very open and honest conversation, between two coaches who perfectly understand, without any hypocrisy, what moments like these mean.

“We spoke at length, very pleasantly, with great mutual respect and admiration, as I’ve said before. I didn’t just speak with Rui, but also with his assistant, Tiago, whom I’ve known for a long time. Sometimes controversy arises when, in reality, things are completely normal.

“I can tell you this story. I was at Milan, we were playing against Roma, and the coach who would replace me had already been hired [Conceiçao]. The next day I had to quickly clear out my room and locker because the new coach wanted to come in.

“And you know what? I didn’t even get a phone call, but there was no need. In football, these situations are part of the game, and I didn’t take it personally. We must understand, without hypocrisy, that these processes are natural.”

#1740. Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

MOISÉS CAICEDO THAT IS INCREDIBLE 🤯 pic.twitter.com/C6CEcUG1sE

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Chelsea conclude their tour of the Far East with a game against Johor Darul Ta’zim on Sunday in Malaysia before returning home.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

The final whistle is blown in Jakarta and Chelsea have cruised to a 3-0 win over AC Milan. Goals from Caicedo and a double from Pedro either side of half-time have led Xabi Alonso’s side to the victory. They have one more game out in the Far East before returning home to the UK.

What a performance! 👏 pic.twitter.com/GcUZXwXbRj

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1739. Inter Milan vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 06 Nov 2026 16:55, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:00

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Ending their 19-game undefeated streak in Serie A, Inter were well beaten by AC Milan in last week's Derby della Madonnina, making it eight straight second-city contests without a win.

With illness sweeping through Cristian Chivu's squad, those fit enough to start were swept aside by the rampant Rossoneri, who surged into an early two-goal lead and eventually won 3-1.

After falling three points behind Lazio, the Nerazzurri had little time to reflect and swiftly switched focus to their ailing European campaign.

Inter had claimed just three points from their opening three Champions League matches, but they were back near their best on Tuesday night, beating Feyenoord 3-0 at De Kuip.

Yann Bisseck put the visitors in front, and Pio Esposito doubled their lead before the break, with Piotr Zielinski adding an excellent third goal in the second half.

As a result, Chivu and co sit 14th in the table midway through this season's league phase, keeping them firmly in contention for the knockout rounds.

Before international football intervenes, they must now face a potential title rival - albeit one whom they have traditionally dominated.

History weighs heavily on Inter's side in this Lombardy derby, having won 14 consecutive Serie A home games against Como, while keeping a clean sheet in eight of the last nine.

Dating back down the decades, Como have lost their last 11 top-flight meetings with Inter, plus a recent Coppa Italia semi-final tie between the two sides.

Very much in demand, head coach Cesc Fabregas has come away empty-handed from each league game against a club that sought to appoint him in the summer of 2025.

Inter tried to lure the Catalan away from Como before hiring Chivu, but going toe-to-toe with the Nerazzurri has brought four straight Serie A defeats by a 12-3 aggregate scoreline.

That sequence includes a chastening 4-0 loss at San Siro last December, but the Biancoblu were unlucky not to reach the cup final after a thrilling semi-final second leg a few months later.

More recently, they have made Europe sit up and take notice with some eye-catching Champions League results, as the debutants followed their 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless destruction of Lens.

Como travelled to France in midweek and left with an emphatic 9-1 victory, top scorer Tasos Douvikas helping himself to a hat-trick in an incredible rout.

That leaves the rookies above the likes of Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Inter in the table, with automatic entry to the last 16 now firmly fixed in their sights.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, they have put together six consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 22 goals and conceding just four.

In Serie A, the Lariani have collected a club record 23 points from their first 10 fixtures, and few would rule them out of vying for the Scudetto.

Though Inter captain Lautaro Martinez is not due back until after the break, and Luis Henrique is also ruled out, the hosts can welcome back a trio of players.

Benjamin Pavard has joined English pair John Stones and Curtis Jones in resuming full training, and they could all make the bench this weekend.

Furthermore, Alessandro Bastoni - who scored in last week's Milan derby - is available after serving a UEFA suspension against Feyenoord.

Up front, Pio Esposito has just netted his first club goal since September, while Marcus Thuram has previously scored four in three league games against Como.

The visitors also boast a potent attack, as Douvikas and star man Nico Paz already have nine Champions League strikes between them.

That pair have been similarly productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined, but Douvikas has failed to find the net in five prior games against Inter.

Once again, Fabregas will be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez, Jayden Addai and Assane Diao due to injury.

J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Bastoni; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Zielinski, Dimarco; Thuram, Esposito

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Kaiki; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

#1738. Report: Is Liverpool player actually good enough? Club is torn

One club is torn on a Liverpool star. Is he actually good enough to justify the money involved?

Alisson Becker's future is up in the air. We certainly don't know what's going to happen with him and we're not sure Liverpool do, either.

His contract expires at the end of the season, of course. It was due to expire last summer but Liverpool triggered a clause that extended things another year. Even with that, speculation that Allisson could join Juventus ran rampant and it's certainly true that the Old Lady pushed to sign the player.

But Alisson stuck around and it's a good thing, too. He remains Liverpool's best goalkeeper and by some distance - if he does leave, the club is up against it to sign someone to even maintain the standards, let alone improve them.

Which is why it's quite strange that a potential destination for Alisson isn't even convinced about signing him.

Alisson Becker's futureAlisson has been linked with a few clubs but two in particular: Juventus and Flamengo. Flamengo, the biggest club in Brazil, feel best-placed to get him back in his native country. However, Sport Witness claim the Brazilians aren’t sure Alisson is actually good enough to justify a move. They cite his performances for the national team as evidence that he’s not the elite-level goalkeeper that many think he is. That, of course, is completely insane. Alisson has won everything at club level and any Liverpool fan who remembers that last few decades would say he’s by far the best goalkeeper the club has had since the formation of the Premier League.

Alisson has been linked with a few clubs but two in particular: Juventus and Flamengo. Flamengo, the biggest club in Brazil, feel best-placed to get him back in his native country.

However, Sport Witness claim the Brazilians aren’t sure Alisson is actually good enough to justify a move. They cite his performances for the national team as evidence that he’s not the elite-level goalkeeper that many think he is.

That, of course, is completely insane. Alisson has won everything at club level and any Liverpool fan who remembers that last few decades would say he’s by far the best goalkeeper the club has had since the formation of the Premier League.

So we’re in a situation where Alisson may not quite have the offers that many thought he would. Does that change things for Liverpool?

There’s surely a scenario here where paying to renew Alisson’s deal makes sense and a lack of competition will naturally drive his wage demands down. We still believe Liverpool will move on because of his age but the natural difficulty in replacing him must keep the door open to a new deal in some respect.

Flamengo fumbling their position makes it easier for Liverpool to do that.

#1736. Marcus Rashford names player closest to Lionel Messi's level

By Naim Beneddra | 06 Nov 2026 16:57

Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has named Lamine Yamal as the most talented footballer he has played alongside, suggesting that the Barcelona teenager could eventually come close to matching Lionel Messi's extraordinary achievements.

The England international spent the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Barcelona, where he developed a close appreciation of Yamal's abilities before returning to Old Trafford during the summer.

Despite having shared a dressing room with some of football's biggest names, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Harry Kane, Rashford believes the 19-year-old possesses a level of natural talent unlike anything he has previously encountered.

Speaking during a question-and-answer session with Manchester United supporters at Old Trafford, the 29-year-old revealed that he had personally told Yamal how highly he rated him before leaving Barcelona.

Rashford went even further by suggesting that the Spanish international could end his career with seven Ballon d'Or awards, an achievement that would place him within touching distance of Messi's record.

Rashford's comments came during an appearance in Manchester United's Ambassadors' Lounge ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma.

The forward, who has been sidelined by injury in recent weeks, was asked about Messi and the prospects of his former Barcelona teammate following the recent Ballon d'Or ceremony.

He explained that he had already spoken directly to Yamal about his abilities before completing his return to Manchester.

"Before I left Barcelona, I told him I'd played with some very talented players, but he was above them all," Rashford said, in comments reported by the Manchester Evening News.

The former Aston Villa loanee was particularly struck by how much Yamal had achieved despite still being a teenager.

"I've never seen a player at that age be as talented as he is," he continued.

"For me, he's the closest somebody can get to the level of Messi over the years."

The comparison carries considerable weight given Rashford's experience at the highest level.

He played alongside Ronaldo during the Portuguese star's second spell at Manchester United and has also shared the pitch with Kane for England.

However, Rashford's assessment was focused on Yamal's exceptional ability at such a young age, rather than suggesting that the Barcelona winger has already surpassed those established stars in terms of career achievements.

The United attacker also made clear that he still considers Messi an almost impossible standard to replicate.

Describing the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner as a complete footballing genius, Rashford acknowledged that another player with the Argentine's full range of abilities may never emerge.

Nevertheless, his admiration for Yamal's potential was unmistakable.

The England international believes the Barcelona youngster possesses the talent to remain among the world's leading players for many years, provided he continues developing at his current rate.

Rashford's prediction about Yamal's future went beyond comparing his playing style and natural ability with Messi.

The Manchester United forward suggested that the teenager could eventually collect seven Ballon d'Or trophies.

"If he goes on to win seven Ballons d'Or, I wouldn't be surprised," Rashford explained.

It was a remarkable assessment of a player who has yet to win the senior award but has already finished among its leading contenders on three occasions.

Yamal placed eighth in 2024, finished runner-up to Ousmane Dembele in 2025 and took third place in October's 2026 ceremony, behind winner Harry Kane and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe.

He also collected his third consecutive Kopa Trophy last month, having won the award for the world's best young player in 2024 and 2025.

The Barcelona star's rapid rise has been accompanied by major collective success.

He played a central role in Spain's Euro 2024 triumph before helping his country win the 2026 World Cup, while also establishing himself as one of the most influential players in Hansi Flick's Barcelona side.

At club level, Yamal has already become a regular match-winner, combining exceptional dribbling ability with increasingly productive contributions in front of goal.

Rashford also took the opportunity to congratulate Kane on his Ballon d'Or success, revealing that he had sent the Bayern Munich striker a personal message after the ceremony.

The United forward felt that Kane's outstanding goalscoring record and creative output made him a deserving winner of the prestigious award.

His support for Kane did not diminish his enthusiasm about Yamal's future, with Rashford clearly viewing the Spaniard's best years as still to come.

For Rashford himself, the comments offer an insight into the lasting impression left by his season in Catalonia.

Barcelona declined to activate the purchase option in his loan agreement, leading to his return to Manchester United, where he is attempting to revive his career under Michael Carrick.

His admiration for Yamal, however, has evidently remained undiminished.

Having witnessed the teenager's qualities at close quarters, Rashford believes the Barcelona number 10 has the potential to build a career that invites comparisons with the greatest players the sport has produced.

#1735. West Ham star's WAG aims brutal parting dig at Nuno Espirito Santo after Hammers sacked under-fire manager - while team-mate 'likes' club post confirming his exit

Published: 03:40 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EDT, 3 November 2026

Nuno Espirito Santo has been sacked by West Ham after a difficult start to the season, with Scott Parker poised to take over.

The Championship promotion favourites are eighth, so far struggling to live up to their billing after being relegated from the Premier League last season.

The former Tottenham, Wolves and Nottingham Forest manager, 52, signed a three-year contract in September 2025 but failed to stop the Hammers from crashing out of the top flight after a poor start to the season.

They were expected to start strongly in the second tier, yet Saturday's 3-1 home defeat by West Bromwich Albion left them with just six wins in 13 matches before Nuno's fate was confirmed on Tuesday morning.

Shortly after that news was confirmed, Marrion Areola, wife of West Ham's back-up keeper Alphonse, aimed a brutal parting dig at Nuno on her Instagram account.

Marrion, who had previously attacked Nuno after last season's relegation for dropping her husband, shared a series of Instagram stories where she appeared to express her joy at the news.

Nuno Espirito Santo has been sacked by West Ham with the club eighth in the Championship

Marrion Areola, wife of West Ham keeper Alphonse, aimed a brutal parting shot at Nuno

In one, she was smiling and posing for a photo, while in another she was skipping through the streets with Sam Phillips' 'Happy' song playing in the background.

In a third story, she shared a video from the famous film Sound of Music of So Long Farewell being sung.

Within the song, which is performed by the seven von Trapp children, a series of lyrics including 'so long', 'farewell', 'good night', 'Auf Wiedersehen', 'Adieu' and 'Au revoir' are mentioned in what is believed to her parting shot at Nuno.

West Ham's Instagram post announcing Nuno's exit, meanwhile, was liked by out of favour Mexican midfielder Edson Alvarez, who is yet to feature in the Championship this season.

George Earthy, a former academy graduate who now plays for Reading, also appeared to like the post.

Back in the summer, Marrion had taken to social media to target Nuno and former boss Graham Potter in a series of posts, blaming the pair for West Ham's relegation and hitting out at the pair for dropping her husband.

Marrion initially shared an image of Areola holding up the Conference League trophy in 2023 and stated: 'From a trophy to relegation. Thank you Potter for the start of this season and Nuno for the end.'

In another, Marrion accused Nuno of dropping her husband - who lost his place to Mads Hermansen - 'for no particular reason'.

'Being dropped at the beginning of the season for no reason,' Marrion wrote. 'Being back after a very bad start and then has made 20 games and all of a sudden: "I'm really sorry - you won't start", "Why?", "For no particular reason but I'm sorry".'

Marrion also shared a post from December that stated Areola had the highest save percentage in the Premier League, before adding on the club's relegation: 'Very sad day for the fans. Very frustrated for the family. But always proud of you no matter what.'

She then placed the blame on Nuno for Areola missing out on France's squad for the World Cup.

Sharing highlights from Areola's five appearances for France's national team she wrote: 'And NO World Cup this year, thank you Nuno'.

Meanwhile, it is understood that Parker is set to replace the Portuguese boss, with the former West Ham midfielder having been out of work since leaving Burnley shortly after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed last season.

Parker, who has won promotion to the top flight as a manager with Fulham, Bournemouth and the Clarets, made 129 appearances for the Hammers between 2007 and 2012, winning three Player of the Year awards during his time at the club.

Former West Ham midfielder Scott Parker is poised to replace Nuno at the London Stadium

Nuno's dismissal comes after the Hammers were beaten 3-1 by West Brom on Saturday

In a club statement on Tuesday morning, West Ham had said: 'West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

'Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

'Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

'West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

'The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.'

The club added that Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville would take temporary charge of the team ahead of Wednesday's trip to Cardiff City.

However, it is believed that Parker will be in charge for that game if a deal is agreed in time, and that Noble, a former team-mate of his, could be part of his backroom team.

Many had expected Nuno to depart in the aftermath of relegation – and Daily Mail Sport understands that Hammers co-owner David Sullivan wanted to part ways with the Portuguese coach – but Daniel Kretinsky, now the club's largest shareholder, backed him to lead the club's promotion charge.

After that decision, the club released a statement outlining their plans and revealed that Nuno was 'highly motivated' for the challenge ahead.

Despite the high-profile sales of Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville in the summer, West Ham kept the likes of Jarrod Bowen, Tomas Soucek, Taty Castellanos and Konstantinos Mavropanos.

They also invested heavily in the squad, which included the addition of Arne Engels from Celtic for a Championship record fee of £22million.

Although they picked up 6-0 victories over Wrexham and Lincoln City, Nuno's side struggled for consistency, and back-to-back defeats by Southampton and West Brom in recent weeks proved to be the final straw.

During and after the defeat by the Baggies, home fans at the London Stadium turned on Nuno and subjected him to chants of 'sacked in the morning'.

Speaking to the media afterwards, Nuno outlined his desire to turn things around.

'Every day there is pressure,' he said. 'I’m disappointed because we wanted to improve things. We want to win matches.

'This (the chants) is the reality. You can only change this if we win games. That’s the solution: getting better results. We have to go back to good performances.

'We dropped points against Burnley (in the season opener), we lost (at home) to Charlton, Southampton and West Brom. The only solution is to improve our game. When we do that, our fans are going to stick with us. They’re going to support us.'

West Ham co-owner David Sullivan had wanted to part ways with Nuno back in the summer

West Ham have suffered back-to-back defeats after last season's Premier League relegation

There is a certain irony to the defeat by West Brom being the end for Nuno given he is a legendary former manager of their arch-rivals Wolves.

But, despite an upturn in form at the back-end of last season and an eight-game unbeaten run earlier in this campaign, he departs the London Stadium with a record of 19 wins, 19 defeats and 15 draws from 53 matches in charge.

After the Cardiff game, West Ham – who are six points adrift of table-toppers Middlesbrough – face a trip to Blackburn before the two-week international break.

#1733. Ferencvaros star Yusuf discusses San Siro opportunity, Amorim’s praise and derby analysis

Ferencvaros striker Bamidele Yusuf is relishing the chance to play against AC Milan at an iconic stadium like San Siro.

For Milan, the task is quite a simple one tonight: they must beat their opponents from Hungary to get back on course in Europe and to keep alive their already slim hopes of getting into the top eight in the table, to get direct last-16 qualification.

However, they are facing a team full of confidence that have not lost in their last 20 games across all competitions. Ferencvaros have also won three out of three in the Europa League too, beating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen and Torreense.

Yusuf spoke at a press conference on the eve of the match against Milan alongside head coach Borbely Balazs. The forward echoes the words if his manager, speaking of the great opportunity a night like this presents.

You have made many sacrifices to get to San Siro…

“When I think back to where I started, it’s truly extraordinary that I can play against one of the best clubs in the world this Thursday. It’s the result of a huge amount of effort, and I’m quite proud of what I’ve achieved. I hope this journey continues for a long time to come.”

Amorim picked you out specifically as a threat to Milan. How does this make you feel? And what is your preferred role?

“Compliments are nice. It means I’m probably doing things the right way. For me, it makes no difference whether I play as a winger or a striker. In both positions, I always try to give my all and have fun on the pitch. It’s certainly significant that a coach of his calibre has mentioned me.”

Did you analyse Milan’s derby win over Inter?

“They played an intense match against Inter, and we analysed the match in detail. However, we can’t draw conclusions based on how the derby unfolded. I’m curious to see how these ninety minutes unfold.”

#1732. Next Crystal Palace manager: Thomas Tuchel’s stance on Anthony Barry is clear amid Pierre Sage uncertainty

By Oliver Thomas | 06 Nov 2026 17:00

England manager Thomas Tuchel has responded to speculation linking his assistant coach Anthony Barry with the Crystal Palace job.

Barry, 40, is reportedly among the frontrunners to succeed current Eagles boss Pierre Sage if the struggling Selhurst Park outfit decide to relieve the Frenchman of his duties.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner in June, but his Crystal Palace side currently sit inside the Premier League relegation zone after losing six of their opening nine games and conceding a division-high 21 goals.

Should the Eagles lose at home to Liverpool on Sunday, the club’s hierarchy may have a big decision to make over whether to stick with under-pressure Sage or bring in a fresh face to turn the club’s fortunes around.

While Tuchel - who announced his latest England squad on Friday - is hopeful that Barry will remain his number two, he is not surprised to see the “highest-level coach” linked with Premier League clubs.

“He’s very important to me,” the German told BBC Radio 5 Live. “I mean, that’s why I did everything I could to convince him to join my staff once we met in Chelsea and join me on my way to Bayern Munich and then in the national team.

“It’s a privilege for me to have him by my side. He’s challenging me, he’s helping me, he makes me better.

“He’s just a fantastic person and the highest-level coach, so I am not surprised that there are rumours around him. I’m not surprised if there were like possibilities for him.”

Barry’s contract with the Football Association runs until the end of the European Championship in 2028 when England will co-host the tournament.

“My understanding, my wish is, of course, that we stay together until minimum until the Euros,” Tuchel added.

“For me, we are by far not finished, and he will always have a place in my in my coaching staff, also after the Euros.

“But, listen, he has to follow also his own path. At the moment, I think that we are an excellent team, and I think that he feels that he’s in a good place where he wants to be.

“As soon as this changes, I think I will be the first to know. At the moment, I don’t know nothing, so I’m pretty confident that he’s in a good place, but I’m not surprised that he has offers.”

Although Barry has never been a senior first-team manager before, he has a wealth of experience as an assistant coach, predominantly working under Tuchel at Chelsea, Bayern Munich and now England.

The Liverpudlian began his coaching career at Accrington Stanley and Wigan Athletic, while he also gained international experience with the Republic of Ireland, Belgium and Portugal, working under Roberto Martinez with the latter two nations.

As well as Barry, Sean Dyche, Thomas Frank, Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards have been linked with the Crystal Palace job amid uncertainty over Sage’s long-term future.

#1730. Man United injury news: Michael Carrick blow, Liverpool boost as key star set to miss Anfield game after international break

By Lewis Nolan | 06 Nov 2026 17:07

Manchester United's Carlos Baleba will miss his side's clash with fierce rivals Liverpool after the international break, Michael Carrick has confirmed.

The Red Devils are set to face Aston Villa on Sunday in the Premier League, but they know they will be without key players for that clash.

Baleba was forced off in the second half of his side's game against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury.

In a press conference, Carrick confirmed that the midfielder would be out for a considerable period, and that he would be on the treatment table beyond the international break.

That news will come as a significant blow to United, who have to face Liverpool at Anfield on November 22 in the Premier League.

Carrick did not give an exact timeline on Baleba's recovery, but he did reveal that he would miss weeks of action.

United have to face Liverpool after the international break, before taking on Sporting Lisbon three days later in Europe.

Before the start of December, the Red Devils also have to take on Brentford, while the club will also face Newcastle United, Coventry City and RB Leipzig in the first eight days of next month.

Carrick's side end December with fixtures against Crystal Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, though perhaps Baleba would be ready to feature in at least some of those games.

United finished in third place last season with 71 points, 11 more than Liverpool managed, and the Merseysiders were arguably fortunate to accumulate as many as they did.

However, a loss against Villa and a defeat at Anfield could leave the Red Devils trailing their rivals by 14 points after just 11 matchweeks.

Baleba is arguably Carrick's only competent midfielder without the ball, and missing him at Anfield makes taking any points from that match much more challenging.

United's inability to make the most of the fact that Liverpool and several other teams like Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea and Manchester City are in transition is concerning.

Losing against Liverpool would compound the failure of the club's hierarchy, and it would arguably be one of the darkest chapters in United's modern history if a loss dropped them into the relegation zone.
