#1708. Brighton & Hove Albion vs Brentford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 06 Nov 2026 18:08, Last updated: 07 Nov 2026 01:19

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton are a surprise team in the Premier League title picture after winning six, drawing one and losing two of their nine top-flight matches this term.

Fabian Hurzeler's side demonstrated they are capable of bettering the Premier League's biggest teams in last Saturday's away meeting with Manchester City, which saw Yasin Ayari score the decisive goal in a 1-0 victory as Brighton got revenge for their EFL Cup loss to the Citizens just a few days earlier.

The victory moved them to within two points of second-placed Man City and kept them within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Brighton's domestic success has been made all the more impressive by the fact they are balancing it with a Conference League campaign, in which their latest outing yielded a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Getafe in Thursday's trip to Spain.

After moving up to fifth spot in the league phase, the Seagulls will now return to the familiar surroundings of the Amex Stadium, where they are yet to lose this season after winning five and drawing one of their six home matches in all competitions.

All five of those wins have produced clean sheets and at least three goals, including a statement 5-0 victory in their most recent home outing against rivals Crystal Palace.

Brighton head into Sunday's fixture with an unbeaten Premier League home record against Brentford, having won three and drawn two of their five top-flight meetings at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford, meanwhile, are sitting two points adrift of the top four after winning three, drawing five and losing just one of their nine Premier League games this season.

While the Bees are firmly in the hunt for European football, they returned from the international break with a four-game winless run in all competitions before they got back on track in last Saturday's home clash with Nottingham Forest.

A Nikola Milenkovic own goal sent Keith Andrews's side into the break with a slender advantage, before Igor Thiago scored in a second straight game to wrap up all three points at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Bees will head on their travels with hopes of recording back-to-back Premier League victories for the first time since beating Aston Villa and Newcastle United at the start of February.

That will be easier said than done for a team that has gone nine consecutive away league games without a win, although they have at least proven to be tough to beat after drawing each of their four Premier League road trips this term.

If they are to claim a long-awaited win, they will have to beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium for the first time since picking up a 2-0 victory in the Championship in September 2016.

The visitors will at least fancy their chances of striking first, having netted the opener in eight of their nine Premier League matches.

Brighton & Hove Albion Premier League form:

Brighton & Hove Albion form (all competitions):

Brighton remain without the services of Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas, Zadok Yohanna and Evan Ferguson.

Pascal Struijk and Femi Azeez are making progress in their respective injury recoveries, but Sunday's contest is likely to come too soon for the pair.

Full-back Ferdi Kadioglu, who has missed the last three games with a hip issue, is understood to have a chance of proving his fitness in time for the home fixture.

If he is ready to feature, the Turkey international will likely replace Costinha in what could be the only change made to the side that started last Saturday's win over Man City.

As for the visitors, Andrews has reported no fresh injury concerns, although he is unable to call upon a number of players, including Rico Henry, Kaye Furo, Josh Dasilva and Fabio Carvalho.

Antoni Milambo has been training regularly as he closes in on a return from a long-term injury absence, but he is not expected to be risked at the Amex Stadium.

The Brentford boss will welcome back Yehor Yarmoliuk, who is in contention for a starting spot after serving a three-match ban.

Jaidon Anthony is also pushing for a starting berth after coming off the bench to provide an assist for Thiago's goal in the win over Nottingham Forest.

Brighton & Hove Albion possible starting lineup:

Verbruggen; Kadioglu, Vuskovic, Dunk, Boscagli; Gross, Andres; Gomez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas

Kelleher; Kayode, Ajer, Van den Berg, Lewis-Potter; Yarmoliuk, Janelt; Anthony, Jensen, Schade; Thiago

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

#1707. From Jose Mourinho's Sevilla disaster to Erik ten Hag's dismal group stage exit: Man United's litany of Champions League humiliations since Sir Alex Ferguson - as Michael Carrick fights for his job ahead of Roma clash

Published: 18:02 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EDT, 3 November 2026

Michael Carrick and Manchester United are enduring the club's worst start to a league season in 40 years, with the Red Devils languishing in 17th place.

Their woes in recent years have been well documented, with the club seemingly incapable of finding anyone to match the glory days under Sir Alex Ferguson.

Since his departure in 2013, they have had eight managers – seven of whom have managed them in Europe's biggest competition.

The three-time champions of Europe have performed particularly poorly in the Champions League in that time, not making it past the quarter-finals once in seven attempts.

They have won less than half of their Champions League fixtures since Ferguson left – and only 34 per cent in the current decade.

Carrick brought United back into the Champions League last season but since being given the permanent role has hit shocking form

And they will be lucky to even reach that stage this season if they continue to play as they have been in the competition, losing to Atletico Madrid away and being embarrassed by Champions League debutants Como.

With United set to take on Roma on Tuesday in their fourth game of the competition, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at how each manager on United's carousel has fared in the Champions League... and where it unravelled for all of them.

It feels as if it has been an age since David Moyes took the reins at Old Trafford. The Scotsman had a torrid time in his ten-month spell at United.

His tenure was characterised by embarrassing losses, a lack of consistency and an inability to transition from the old regime.

Moyes was sacked in April after a 2-0 loss to his old Everton side that ended United's hopes of a top-four finish for that season. He was already under serious pressure having been dumped out of the Champions League in the quarter-finals by Bayern Munich.

Moyes was handpicked by Ferguson to replace him but didn't even last a season at United

The current Everton manager oversaw a 1-1 draw at home in the first leg, with Nemanja Vidic's goal being cancelled out by Bastian Schweinsteiger – who moved to Old Trafford a year later. But Bayern – managed by Pep Guardiola – quickly responded to Patrice Evra's goal in the second leg to win it 3-1.

They had to battle to even get that far, with a comfortable group stage – four wins and two draws – being followed by an embarrassing 2-0 defeat at Olympiacos in the first leg of the last 16. A Robin van Persie hat-trick in the second leg spared their blushes.

The big Dutchman came to United with a stellar CV having won both the Champions League and UEFA Cup with Ajax in the 90s, as well as league titles in Spain and Germany.

And he seemed the exact kind of serial winner who would be the perfect replacement for Ferguson, but it just didn't work out. Van Gaal spent heavily in the market when he arrived - most notably breaking the British transfer record to secure the services of Angel Di Maria for £59.7million - but he simply couldn't find his feet in England.

Van Gaal had just the one season in the Champions League with United before leaving, and it was possibly the most disastrous since Ferguson's departure.

They were placed in a group with Wolfsburg, PSV and CSKA Moscow, and were dumped out at the earliest possible stage, finishing third in the group with just eight points. They fell into the Europa League and - after overturning a disastrous 2-1 defeat by Danish side Midtjylland in the first leg of their last-32 game - were sent packing by Liverpool.

Joining in 2016 after being sacked by Chelsea, Jose Mourinho immediately got busy in the market.

And initially it seemed as if he was going to make it work. Paul Pogba and Zlatan Ibrahimovic arrived and United won their first three games. Although their league form dipped, they did go on to win the League Cup and the Europa League in that first season.

But then it all began to fall away. Like Van Gaal and Moyes before him, Mourinho only got one try at his favourite competition with United, and exited in a less than graceful manner.

Jose won the Europa League whilst in Manchester but never really found success in the big competition

He may have won it with Porto in 2004 and Inter six years later but at United he only got as far as the round of 16, and crashed out after a 2-1 home defeat by Sevilla following a 0-0 draw in the first leg.

Recently Jose revealed that his relationship with the Red Devils was very nearly different. In his new Netflix biopic, Mourinho, he said that he had agreed to take over straight after Ferguson - only to be lured back to Chelsea by Roman Abramovich instead. Who knows how he would have fared at Old Trafford if he had joined three years earlier.

Mourinho's successor also had an excellent start to life in the United dugout but ended up being hounded out after a tumultuous three years.

When Ole was at the wheel, at first it seemed like United were on course to return to the big time however, slowly but surely, it became clear that it wasn't going to work out.

Solskjaer is one of two men on this list to have won the Champions League with United as a player and the Norwegian scored arguably the most historic goal in United's European history, getting the dramatic winner in the 1999 final.

And he is probably the only gaffer since Ferguson to have had a positive memorable moment in the competition. It came in Paris in March of 2019, shortly after he took over. After losing 2-0 at home in the first leg of the tie they looked like they were already out but miraculously Ole masterminded a 3-1 victory and won on away goals.

Unfortunately that is where the good times as a manager in the Champions League end. After the PSG win United were beaten 4-0 on aggregate by Barcelona and then didn't make it into the competition for the 2019-20 season.

They did return with Ole in 2020-21 - only to be knocked out in the group stage, finishing third in a group with PSG, RB Leipzig and Turkish side Basaksehir. They went on to reach the Europa League final that year - losing to Villarreal on penalties - and Solskjaer was gone in November, before the end of next season's group stage.

Taking over as interim manager until the end of the 2021-22 campaign - following a caretaker spell from a certain Michael Carrick - Austrian Rangnick was in charge for just three European games.

The final game of the group stage saw a 1-1 draw with Swiss side Young Boys, with Mason Greenwood scoring United's goal.

Then they took on Atletico Madrid in the last-16, and after a 1-1 draw away, were sent packing with a 1-0 second-leg defeat at Old Trafford.

Renan Lodi's header for Atletico Madrid sent United crashing out under Ralf Rangnick

Rangnick's spell at United is best remembered for his forthright assessments of the club's dire situation, and he famously likened their situation to that of a patient needing open-heart surgery.

'You don’t even need glasses to see and analyse where the problems are,' he said. 'Now it’s about how do we solve them? It’s not enough to do some minor amendments. In medicine you would say that this is an operation of the open heart.

'If this happens and everyone has realised that this has to happen and if people want to work together then it makes sense and I believe it doesn’t take two or three years to change those things. This can happen within one year.'

More than four years on, the fans are still waiting.

Erik ten Hag came in nine years after Ferguson's exit, and while he brought a League Cup and an FA Cup to Old Trafford it was not enough to stop him being sacked.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League. He actually fared even worse than his predecessors by finishing rock bottom of the group in the 2023-24 season, after particularly rough losses away to Copenhagen and Galatasaray.

Like Van Gaal and Solskjaer, Ten Hag's United failed to make it past the group stage of the Champions League

After a dismal eighth-placed finish in the Premier League the FA Cup win over Manchester City ended that season on a high - and saved Ten Hag's job.

He even signed a contract extension that summer, but was ditched by October with United 14th.

Ruben Amorim, who replaced Ten Hag, did not manage United in the Champions League - though he did reach the Europa League final with them in 2025.

His sacking in January this year paved the way for Michael Carrick to join as interim and, in steering them to third place, ensured United were back at Europe's top table after two seasons away.

That also won him the permanent role, but Carrick has had a torrid start to the new campaign - winning just two of his side's 13 games in all competitions and setting a new club record for the longest winless streak in the Premier League era (nine).

One of those wins was in the Champions League against Azerbaijani minnows Sabah, but they followed that with the defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como.

Carrick will hope United can finally arrest this run of form at home to Roma on Tuesday, but it will not be easy with the Italians enjoying an excellent start to the season and currently sitting third in Serie A.

A win, however, could keep Carrick in a job and breathe some life into a United team that desperately needs it.

#1706. Report: Andoni Iraola is about to miss out on Liverpool's next Virgil van Dijk

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool's head coach has been a bit mixed.

While the Spaniard may have only lost three games across all competitions this season, it still feels like the Reds could have done a lot better than they have.

They should have put up a much tougher fight against Manchester City and Arsenal than they did but, because they didn't, they're now fifth in the Premier League table.

Wednesday's 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce proved how far the Reds still have to go before they're treated as genuine challengers for silverware again.

So, in order to push them towards achieving this goal, the January transfer window may have to be a busy one with the Reds already being linked with many different moves.

Chelsea want to offer long-term Liverpool target Levi Colwill a new contract

Liverpool's defence may have had a lot of work done to it in the summer but, there are still several changes that need to be made before its back to its best.

Virgil van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo have all performed to a fairly high standard but, with Van Dijk's contract set to expire in June 2028, change is clearly afoot.

Indeed, the Reds could end up offering the Dutchman a new deal but, right now, that doesn't feel all that likely.

This has led to several different players being linked with a Liverpool move with some causing genuine excitement to emerge from fans.

However, as per a fresh update from TEAMtalk, one of the Reds' long-term targets, Levi Colwill, looks likely to be offered an extension to his current terms with Chelsea.

"Chelsea are ready to open discussions with Levi Colwill over a new contract, with an extension for their homegrown defensive star expected to become a priority in 2027 amid interest from Liverpool, TEAMtalk understands," they wrote.

"The Blues are keen to secure the long-term future of the 23-year-old, who has established himself as one of the Premier League’s most impressive young defenders since breaking into the first team in 2023.

"Brighton were particularly keen to secure Colwill on a permanent basis following his successful loan spell at the Amex Stadium, but Chelsea made it clear they had no intention of selling.

"Tottenham and Liverpool have also made approaches for the England international, only to encounter a similar stance from the Blues.

Levi Colwill would have been perfect for Liverpool

Not only do Liverpool need extra depth among their ranks right now but, they also need to add a fair few homegrown players to their ranks.

Thanks to how many foreign players the Reds have in their squad, they physically can't register anymore players other than homegrown ones.

This is obviously a massive problem with Wataru Endo and Federico Chiesa both missing out on all of their Champions League games as they're not registered to play.

Colwill is one of many centre-backs who would have been a solid acquisition for Liverpool.

However, there's just something about the Englishman that makes him feel like a perfect successor for Van Dijk.

He's tall, fast and strong. Three of the key things about Van Dijk's game.

And, since he's only 23 years old and has already featured in 86 Premier League games, there's plenty of room for him to grow while already having a decent chunk of experience under his belt.

Here's hoping that the Blues don't actually offer the versatile defender a new deal so that the Reds can finally get their man.

#1705. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1704. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.

#1703. Man United news: Lisandro Martinez should not play for the Red Devils again

By Matt Law | 06 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 18:31

Ahead of Manchester United's Premier League clash with Aston Villa on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses the 20-time English champions.

The Red Devils are without a win in the Premier League since the end of August but managed to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

If they go and get beaten here, it undoes all the good work from the Roma match. It was just an extraordinary game. Those two goals going in, the Soule goal and then the Malen penalty, and you just thought here we go again.

As Mick McCarthy said, it can get worse. At half time, that was probably as bad as I have felt as a Man United fan for a while. There have been some bad moments over the last 14 or 15 years, but you just thought they were never going to win a game again.

Then you have a turning moment, and it was the Fernandes penalty: he missed it, then the retake, and it goes in. It just takes little moments in football.

Roma have previous in the Champions League this season of not being able to hold on to a lead. It was happening against Real Madrid as well. They must have smelt blood. They must have felt Roma had mistakes in them. It was not Roma's first-choice goalkeeper between the sticks either. They did not test him in the first half at all.

But then the penalty goes in, and you think: what are they made of? Cunha was one that took the game by the scruff of the neck, quite literally late on.

He took his shirt off for the yellow card and then got sent off with a bad tackle late on, but you do not mind that. The fans certainly do not mind seeing that aggression, which has been lacking all season.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right for this game. Amad Diallo is a good footballer, nice and tidy, but he has not scored a goal in going on a year now, and that is just not good enough. He missed a big one at Chelsea last weekend.

Shea Lacey has to come in down the right. He played that lovely pass to Cunha for the 3-2 goal late on. He was bright, he wanted the ball, and he has to come into the team.

Patrick Dorgu is back in training, and it will be very interesting to see whether he is fit enough to start. If he is, I would like to see a reshuffle at the back: Dorgu at left back, Dalot over to the right, with Yoro and Maguire in the middle.

Martinez is suspended, and Heaven is struggling at the moment. I do not want to go too overboard on Heaven. He has had a lot of criticism, but he is only 20 years old and is just not ready, probably not good enough, to be a starting centre back at Man United at this moment in time, and that is fine. He can supplement the squad.

Carlos Baleba will be facing a lengthy period out. Tielemans as a straight swap, or Santos as an option alongside Kobbie Mainoo. Mbeumo, Cunha and Fernandes: I expect them to start again.

I do not think there will be too many changes, but I would like to see those ones because they just need more down the right, where the fullbacks have struggled this season.

The defeat to Chelsea: Man United played really well in the first half but just could not get that goal. They did get a goal through Cunha that was rightly disallowed for offside, but it was so disappointing at that moment.

The Martinez incident: I said a few weeks ago after his comments about the Champions League game that I did not want him to play for the club again, and I do not want him to play for the club again now. That was unforgivable. He has lost his head. He is going to leave the club, whether that is this summer or the next.

Whether you release him or look to sell him, I do not want Martinez playing for Man United anymore. He has let the club down badly and there is no coming back from that.

Try to get a centre back in January, and next summer Man United need to sign three or four defenders. Can Marcus Rashford get himself fit for this game? Probably unlikely. Luke Shaw is still out. Sesko is still out.

But there is a chance now for them to go and beat Aston Villa, a good Aston Villa side, on Sunday afternoon, and then go into the international break in a positive mood.

I read a report recently that apparently Didier Deschamps has been contacted as a potential name, one that has not been at the forefront of many people's thoughts at this stage.

I still expect Carrick to leave at some point, whether that is after this game, in two months' time, or at the end of the season.

I do not expect Michael Carrick to be the manager of Manchester United for the next five years.

The reports at the moment suggest there would not be an interim, so it is unlikely he will go and then someone be brought in next summer.

It looks like they might try to keep Carrick in the job for as long as possible until they identify that next appointment. I wrote a piece recently about Cesc Fabregas and Man United.

After that Como win in the Champions League, I would like to see Fabregas as a long-term option at Manchester United. Deschamps would be a very interesting candidate as well.

Carrick got his stay of execution last time out. He needed that result, and inside he would have been absolutely buzzing with what he saw in that second half.

Man United cannot go two down in this game. If they go two-nil down, they are in big trouble. They need to score first on Sunday.

Go and get a win, go into the international break with more positivity ahead of the Liverpool game at Anfield straight after. Big games to come: Sporting Lisbon away in the Champions League at the end of the month.

I expect Carrick to stay at the moment. If they get beaten here and it is a bad one, he could go. Really interesting times, but a good win last time out and finally a little bit of positivity.

#1702. GdS: Milan’s €500m Adidas deal causes reaction from rivals Inter – the situation

Inter are looking enviously at their city rivals AC Milan once again after Saturday’s derby, with the news of the record Adidas deal emerging.

As reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport on Wednesday, under the new agreement Adidas will pay Milan €50m per year for ten seasons starting from 2028-29. This is when the collaboration with PUMA ends, who currently pay €24.5m per year, as per the last accounts.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The paper (via Calciomercato.com) go on to state that it is likely that the €50m yearly figure includes sporting bonuses, such as participation in the Champions League, the value of material supplies (value in kind) and a portion to be invested in promotional activities (marketing fund).

Contracts with kit makers are not limited to recognising the value of just the home, away, third and other shirts, but can extend to the sale of related products. Then, guaranteed minimums and royalties come into play that are triggered above a certain turnover threshold.

For example, in addition to the €24.5m from PUMA, €55.8m in revenues came from store, e-commerce and merchandising/licensing activities, in particular those relating to the contract with the same German company and those from licensing with Fanatics and MatchWornShirt.

As for Inter, the renewal with Nike – effective from 2023 – resulted in a 70% increase over the previous contract, but the €28m per year is not in line with the club’s current commercial value. In addition to the Milan-Adidas deal, Juventus currently get €46m per year from Adidas (€41m from 2027-28).

Inter have maintained their merchandising revenues internally, over €35m in 2025-26 thanks to the new business model introduced with Fanatics, but Nike’s €28m is too little according to the Nerazzurri’s commercial management.

The contract expires in 2031, and La Gazzetta report that they will seek to renegotiate the deal to avoid accumulating delays over the next five years. Considering that Juventus and Milan have committed to the next decade, Inter have leverage as the only one of the ‘big three’ up for grabs.

#1701. Caykur Rizespor vs BB Erzurumspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:55

Caykur Rizespor will be looking to end their five-match winless run when they welcome BB Erzurumspor to Caykur Didi Stadium on Sunday, with the visitors hoping to return to winning ways after suffering a home defeat in their previous Super Lig outing.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 11 points from 10 matches, three points behind the 11th-placed visitors, who have collected 14 points.

Rizespor's recent results have left Recep Ucar with plenty to address, as his side were held to a goalless draw by Kocaelispor last time out, although that point came after three consecutive defeats against Trabzonspor, Corum and Fenerbahce.

Their winless run began with a draw against Goztepe, marking a significant decline from their opening five league matches, during which they recorded three victories.

Their struggles at home are an even more pressing concern, with Rizespor losing all four of their matches at Caykur Didi Stadium this season, conceding 10 goals and scoring just three, leaving them as the only team in the league yet to collect a point on home soil.

They will make another attempt to change that record in what will be their first top-flight meeting with Erzurumspor since 2021, with both sides having recorded one victory each in their four previous Super Lig encounters, alongside two draws.

Erzurumspor won the most recent meeting between the teams, securing a 2-0 victory in the Turkish Cup earlier this year, and are unbeaten in their last two encounters with the hosts (W1, D1).

However, the Serkan Ozbalta's men arrive after suffering a 3-1 home defeat to Corum, which ended a four-match unbeaten run across all competitions (W3, D1).

They will be eager to bounce back immediately on the road, having recorded a positive result in their most recent away fixture, a 3-1 victory over Gaziantep that also marked their first away win of the campaign.

Erzurumspor have also won just once in four previous visits to this ground, losing twice and drawing once, suggesting that Sunday's encounter could prove difficult despite Rizespor's poor home form.

Rizespor are expected to be without Khusniddin Alikulov, who is recovering from a knee injury, while Can Bozdogan is also unavailable with an ankle problem.

Modibo Sagnan is suspended, leaving Ucar with defensive adjustments to make, while Ahmed Kutucu has also been listed as a potential absentee, although his availability remains uncertain.

Erzurumspor are likely to be without Mustafa Yumlu, who is struggling with a muscle injury, although the visitors otherwise appear to have fewer significant availability concerns.

The visitors have scored nine goals in their opening 10 league matches, with Eren Tozlu and Miguel Cardoso contributing three apiece, and both forwards will be hoping to add to their tallies as they prepare to lead the attack.

Caykur Rizespor possible starting lineup:

Gorgen; Pala, Mocsi, Bakayoko, Ariss; Diakite; Mebude, Olawoyin, Laci, Bulut; Gennaro Borrelli

Taskiran; Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Kirtay, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Baiye, Owusu, Rodriguez; Cardoso, Tozlu

With neither side particularly convincing defensively, a closely contested draw looks a reasonable outcome, especially given Rizespor's difficulty turning home advantage into victories.

Erzurumspor have shown enough quality on their travels to trouble the hosts, but their own recent setback suggests they may have to settle for a point.

#1700. Martin O'Neill's greatest mistake was staying after winning the league

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:24 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 14:51 EDT, 3 November 2026

Winning the league title in such dramatic fashion on the final day of last season, Martin O’Neill should have recognised the moment for what it was. The End.

In a chaotic season where he had rescued Celtic from oblivion not once but twice, that was the moment when the credits should have rolled.

The blockbuster Hollywood finale. The perfect opportunity to go out in a blaze of glory and sail off into the sunset, his legacy not only secure but further enhanced.

His decision to stay on as manager this season has proven to be a mistake. In his heart of hearts, O’Neill must realise this. The whole thing is done. Finished. Finito. Terminado, as one of his predecessors would have said.

On the back of the 2-0 defeat to Falkirk last weekend, it has now reached the point where O’Neill’s continued presence at the club is damaging his legacy.

The fans are turning on him. They don’t care what he did for the club 20-odd years ago. They aren’t interested in his wisecracks. They don’t want to hear nostalgic tales of old about how things used to be.

They care only about the here and now and about what they are watching on the pitch. Now mired in a run of three wins in their last ten matches, O’Neill’s side are, if anything, actually getting worse.

O’Neill’s argument about still being top of the league is one of deflection, denial and delusion. Complete and utter claptrap. It is an insult to the intelligence of Celtic supporters.

Martin O'Neill's Celtic team lead the table but have struggled to convince

This is the problem. If there is solid evidence to support the claims that he has lost the faith of the players, then he is also rapidly losing the faith of the fans.

In a way, it is sad that it should come to this. The man is 74 years old. He didn’t ask to be thrust back into the spotlight. At least, not initially.

On two occasions, he answered an SOS call from Dermot Desmond last season. He came back and he did exactly what was asked of him.

If Celtic had any sort of competent succession plan in place, there wouldn’t even have been a conversation around O’Neill’s future towards the end of last season.

It would have been a case of shaking his hand, thanking him enormously for a heroic contribution, before being serenaded by supporters one last time after winning a league and cup double.

Yet, going back to those final few weeks of last season, it was clear O’Neill had the bug for it once again. He was never going to walk away, and nor were the board ever going to turn him down.

In the end, the situation needed one of two things to happen. It either needed O’Neill to save himself from his own desires, and have some sense and foresight about how the club was being run, or it needed Celtic to show some vision and make a proper long-term appointment.

In the absence of both, it was the blind leading the blind. O’Neill hung around primarily to have another crack at Europe, the Celtic board thought they had a bulletproof shield by retaining the services of a club icon.

The argument that kept on being trotted out at the time centred on how winning the league title meant that O’Neill had earned the right to stay on.

But that fundamentally missed the point. Of course he had earned the right. He’s Martin O’Neill. Only Jock Stein stands above him in the pantheon of the club’s all-time greatest managers.

Fans adored him (yes, past tense). But just because he had earned the right doesn’t mean it was the right thing to do. That’s the key difference.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill lifts the league trophy back in May

Whenever Manchester United inevitably sack Michael Carrick, let’s suppose for a second that Sir Alex Ferguson comes in and takes charge for a few games.

Everything goes well, the team start winning games again, everyone starts getting those old feelings coming back.

But would it mean that the right thing to do is to hand Sir Alex the job for another season? Of course it wouldn’t.

The failure to separate that nostalgia and love for O’Neill from what was required moving into this season was a catastrophic error of judgment on Celtic’s part.

The club had absolutely no idea how to move forward in the summer – just like they would have absolutely no idea who to appoint now if O’Neill was to be relieved of his duties.

In the past, Celtic sacked Tommy Burns. They sacked Billy McNeill. The belief that O’Neill could not suffer a similar fate is hugely naive.

Right now, a growing section of the fanbase view him as little more than an extension of Desmond. His status as a club icon is fading.

Over the weekend, a couple of articles surfaced from a few years ago when O’Neill was sacked as Nottingham Forest manager in 2019.

They spoke of how O’Neill eventually lost the dressing room and of how the players were left bemused by his lack of detail on the tactical side of the game.

Some Celtic fans view O'Neill as little more than an extension of major shareholder Dermot Desmond

The parallels with this current Celtic side are obvious. Just look at the comments from Callum McGregor and Cameron Carter-Vickers over recent weeks.

They are a team with absolutely no tactical identity – and it’s difficult to see how this gets any better for as long as O’Neill, along with coaches Shaun Maloney and Mark Fotheringham, remain at the helm.

O’Neill attended a Q&A session at a supporter’s club in Greenock on Monday night, along with chief executive Michael Nicholson and chairman Brian Wilson.

A bizarre announcement from Celtic yesterday claimed that the questioning had been ‘hard but fair’ as supporters voiced their concerns about the current malaise.

The one man who continues to dodge the Paxman treatment is, of course, Desmond himself, the club’s largest shareholder who operates as the commander-in-chief.

And the one question which is now becoming painfully unavoidable is this: what grounds are there for Martin O’Neill to continue as Celtic manager?

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:56

Fenerbahce will be looking to build on an important European victory when they travel to face Corum Belediyespor at Corum Stadyumu in the Turkish Super Lig on Sunday.

Former captain Emre Belozoglu returned to the club as head coach earlier this week, taking charge of a side sitting sixth in the table with 16 points from 10 matches, level on points with their hosts, who occupy seventh place.

Corum have made a respectable start to life in the Super Lig, winning half of their 10 league matches this season to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

After failing to win any of their opening three fixtures, the Red-Black have gone on to collect five victories in their last seven matches, with their most recent success coming in a 3-1 win away to Erzurumspor.

That victory followed their defeat to Goztepe, continuing a recent pattern in which they have responded to each of their last two league defeats with a win in their subsequent fixture.

Burak Yilmaz's side will nevertheless be aware that their defensive organisation faces a much sterner examination on Sunday, having conceded 16 goals in their opening 10 league matches, the most of any team in the top eight, although only four sides have scored more than their 21 goals.

They have scored just six of those goals at home and conceded four, while drawing two and losing two of their four matches at Corum Stadyumu this season.

Sunday's encounter will be the first meeting between the two sides, and Corum will hope to make a positive start to this new fixture, although doing so will require them to record consecutive home victories for the first time this season.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive with renewed confidence after recovering from a difficult spell to beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League, with Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi all finding the net.

That result followed consecutive 2-1 defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray in the Super Lig, a difficult run that preceded Ismail Kartal's departure and Belozoglu's decision to leave Kasimpasa for a second spell in charge of the Yellow Canaries.

The new coach inherits a side that has produced some impressive attacking performances, with only Amed SK (25) scoring more goals than Fenerbahce (24) in the Super Lig, although their inability to turn that attacking quality into consistent victories has left them with five wins from 10 league matches and nine points behind leaders Galatasaray.

Another concern heading into Sunday's clash is their recent away form, having lost their last two competitive matches on the road and conceded in both, with their most recent setback coming against Galatasaray in the league.

Çorum Belediyespor Turkish Super Lig form:

Corum will be without Gokhan Sazdagi, who is suspended after picking up a booking in the victory over Erzurumspor.

Emircan Gurluk is also sidelined with a muscle injury, while Fredy remains a doubt after struggling with a similar problem.

Jesus Ramirez has been one of Corum's most reliable attacking players, scoring six league goals this season, and is expected to lead the line alongside Ermin Mahmic.

Fenerbahce also have several selection concerns, with Nathan Ake and Marco Asensio carrying injuries, while Jayden Oosterwolde is expected to miss out with an Achilles problem.

Archie Brown is suspended following his involvement in the post-match physical brawl against Fenerbahce, while Kojo Peprah Oppong remains a doubt.

One of Belozoglu's biggest decisions will be who leads the attack, with Romelu Lukaku competing with Muriqi, who has scored seven league goals this season and also found the net in the Champions League victory.

Çorum Belediyespor possible starting lineup:

Felipe; Sazdagi, Soyuncu, Smolcic, Borza; Under, Ramadani, Diomande, Kyziridis; Mahmic, Ramirez

Ederson; Semedo, Skriniar, Peprah, Mercan; Kante, Guendouzi; Kahveci, Yuksek, Greenwood; Lukaku

Corum have enough attacking quality to make this an uncomfortable afternoon for Fenerbahce, but the visitors should have sufficient depth and quality to find a way through.

Their confidence will also be boosted by the important European victory in midweek, and we expect Belozoglu to make a winning start to his second spell in charge.

#1696. Awful, Real Madrid are going to rob Liverpool of their next superstar - opinion

Real Madrid look all but certain to rob Liverpool of someone who could be their next superstar. There may be no way to fight back.

Real Madrid have a knack for ruining Liverpool transfer plans. Sometimes that's swooping in to sign a player from Liverpool, like Trent Alexander-Arnold or Ibrahima Konate.

Or, more usually, it's them signing someone that the Reds have spent quite some time working on a deal for. You can actually look at half their first-team to find such players, from Aurelien Tchouameni to Kylian Mbappe to Jude Bellingham to Eduardo Camavinga to...

But now there's a new and fascinating way that they could ruin a transfer plan. Robbing Liverpool of their big Virgil van Dijk replacement.

Jacobo Ramon is the one to watchThere are few players we're higher on than Jacobo Ramon. Our Value Adder data model rates him as one of the most outstanding defenders in Europe last season at just 21 - and he looks even better this term. Ramon was fantastic again this week as Como thrashed RC Lens 9-1 in the UEFA Champions League. He led the match for defensive actions, won all of his duels, picked up an assist, and played a truly ridiculous 18 line-breaking passes from centre-back. It's enough that we've got him down as the ideal replacement for Virgil van Dijk - a player who needs signing very soon. Whether Van Dijk renews his contract or not.

There are few players we're higher on than Jacobo Ramon. Our Value Adder data model rates him as one of the most outstanding defenders in Europe last season at just 21 - and he looks even better this term.

Ramon was fantastic again this week as Como thrashed RC Lens 9-1 in the UEFA Champions League. He led the match for defensive actions, won all of his duels, picked up an assist, and played a truly ridiculous 18 line-breaking passes from centre-back.

It's enough that we've got him down as the ideal replacement for Virgil van Dijk - a player who needs signing very soon. Whether Van Dijk renews his contract or not.

But there's a problem. The more impressive Ramon looks, the more likely it is that Real Madrid simply trigger their buyback clause and use him for themselves.

We're still crossing our fingers that they'll sell once they pay that €9m clause next summer. They've invested in Konate and Dean Huijsen, after all, which opens the door to a sale for big money.

And given this is a player Liverpool were reportedly 'blown away' by earlier this year, we think the Reds would be happy to pay big money for him. We're begging them to.

Ramon feels like a generational centre-back, much as Van Dijk did back in 2017. Signing him with the promise of replacing an all-time great surely seduces him, too, let alone the promise of playing alongside Jeremy Jacquet long-term.

But as we say, Real Madrid hold the cards here and they're on course to rob Liverpool of this signing before it's even off the ground.

#1695. Alanyaspor vs Trabzonspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 06 Nov 2026 18:56

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt a worrying run of results when they welcome Trabzonspor to Alanya Oba Stadium on Sunday, while the visitors have an opportunity to strengthen their position near the top of the Turkish Super Lig table.

The hosts sit 12th with 12 points from 10 matches, whereas the Black Sea Storm occupy third place on 22 points after winning seven of their opening 10 league fixtures.

Alanyaspor suffered a 5-0 defeat away to Genclerbirligi last time out, extending their losing run to three consecutive league matches following earlier setbacks against Kocaelispor and Fenerbahce.

They have conceded 10 goals across those three matches, a significant decline from their previous four-game unbeaten run, during which they recorded two victories and two draws while conceding just three goals.

Their only positive result in recent weeks came in the Turkish Cup, where they beat Bingol 4-1 to end a three-match winless run on home soil.

However, Joao Pereira's side are without a victory in their last three league matches at Alanya Oba Stadium, drawing twice and losing their most recent game against Kocaelispor, with their only home league victory this season coming against Besiktas.

Alanyaspor will hope to show greater resilience on Sunday, particularly given their recent record in this fixture, having remained unbeaten in their last three competitive meetings with Trabzonspor, recording one win and two draws.

Their home record against the visitors is even more impressive, with the hosts unbeaten in their last four matches at Alanya Oba Stadium (W3, D1), while they have lost just twice in their last 10 home meetings, winning five and drawing three.

Trabzonspor, meanwhile, arrive in impressive domestic form, with no side collecting more points than them across the last five league matches, having maintained a perfect record during that period.

They recorded a 2-0 victory over Gaziantep in their most recent league outing, extending a winning run that also includes victories over Caykur Rizespor, Besiktas, Samsunspor and Galatasaray.

That five-match league winning streak formed part of a seven-game run of victories across all competitions, but their momentum was halted on Thursday when the Black Sea Storm suffered a 1-0 home defeat to Freiburg in the Conference League.

Thomas Reis will hope that setback proves to be only a minor distraction as his side look to maintain their domestic form and close the three-point gap to league leaders Galatasaray.

They can also take encouragement from their recent performances away from home, having recorded three consecutive victories on the road across all competitions, a significant improvement after failing to win any of their first four away matches of the season.

Alanyaspor are expected to be without Paolo Fernandes, who has been struggling with a muscle injury, while defender Fatih Aksoy is also a doubt after missing the defeat to Genclerbirligi.

Their potential absences would be a concern for Pereira, particularly after his side conceded five goals in Ankara, where Bedirhan Ozyurt replaced Aksoy in the back three.

Gaius Makouta, Maestro and Baran Gezek are expected to feature in midfield, while Ruan and Florent Hadergjonaj should occupy the wing-back positions.

Trabzonspor have a longer list of potential absentees, with Arseniy Batagov, Ruslan Malinovskyi, Okay Yokuslu and Aral Simsir all listed among the players who could miss out.

Cihan Canak and Franculino are further concerns for Reis, while Sidny Lopes Cabral is available again after missing the European fixture through suspension.

Ernest Muci leads the Super Lig assist charts with six this season and will be looking to create further opportunities for Mohamed Salah, who has scored eight league goals, one fewer than joint-top scorers Victor Osimhen and Gift Orban.

Victor; Lima, Ozyurt, Aliti; Hadergjonaj, Makouta, Gezek, Maestro, Ruan; Kaya, Cedric

Onana; Pina, Savic, Nwaiwu, Lopes Cabral; Fabinho, Kabasakal; Saviolo, Muci, Salah; Onuachu

Trabzonspor's European defeat is a reminder that they are not invulnerable, but their domestic consistency and greater attacking firepower should give them the edge.

Although Alanyaspor have a strong recent record at home in this fixture, their current defensive struggles make it difficult to back them against one of the division's most in-form sides, and we expect the visitors to claim all three points.

#1694. Shambolic off the park, shambolic on it, dire defeat at Falkirk leaves O'Neill on thin ice

Published: 10:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:06 EDT, 3 November 2026

It took Celtic supporters the best part of half an hour on Sunday afternoon to belt out their now traditional rendition of ‘Sack the Board, Sack the Board’.

But as dysfunctional as this club may be off the park, there’s no doubt things are every bit as bad on it. This is an organisation that requires a rebuild from top to bottom. No one should be exempt.

Not the board members, not the management team, not the players. The whole thing is a shambles.

The table will show the champions are right on track to defend their crown. Indeed, the stats here will show this was a contest they dominated. But anyone with a set of eyes and any sort of common sense knows the real story.

Ahead of the match, Martin O’Neill insisted he is essentially oblivious to the outside noise around his team. Aye right.

Callum McGregor looks frustrated as Celtic go down in Falkirk

Scott Tanser celebrates his goal with Falkirk team-mate Owen Eames

Legend at the club though he may be, the Northern Irishman is surely on thin ice. Any other Celtic manager with three wins in his last 10 in all competitions certainly would be.

Frankly, he’s kidding himself on when he says he’s been satisfied with Celtic’s start to the season. The fans aren’t buying that nonsense any more. Does the man himself even believe it?

He continually talks about how his team need time to find their feet. More drivel. We’re now in November. Falkirk also signed 17 in the summer and they seem to be doing relatively well.

The football is just atrocious to watch. It has been all season. Such is the standard of the opposition in Scotland, they usually have just about enough quality to get away with it.

But that’s not a long-term solution to an increasingly worrying problem.

Falkirk, by the way, were outstanding here. They have now won four games on the bounce, each in a thoroughly un-Falkirk way.

Their success under John McGlynn has been built on the ability to pass teams off the park. This victory was far more to do with grit, determination and unity than anything else. Three qualities their opponents are lacking.

Falkirk play like a team. Celtic play like a bunch of individuals. And unless something changes pronto, things are going to get even uglier.

Just as they did in the 2-1 win over Hibernian at Easter Road last week, Celtic fell behind early doors.

Finley Barbrook picked up a loose ball midway inside the visitors’ half before finding Ryan Strain in acres of space on the right-hand side.

The full-back’s cross should have been blootered clear by Cameron Carter-Vickers at the back post with minimal fuss. Goodness knows what he actually tried to do, with the ball simply bouncing off the big American and right into the path of the grateful Ethan Ross, who couldn’t miss from five yards out.

Celtic winger Haissem Hassan gets involved in a scuffle with Falkirk players

Shocking stuff from a Celtic perspective. Carter-Vickers’ comments questioning Celtic’s ‘random’ style following defeats to Rangers in September were bang on the money. But he would do well to examine his own performances too. He’s not as good as some fans seem to think.

It took 10 minutes for Celtic to muster up a response. Liam Scales’ long ball found Camilo Duran in behind the Falkirk defence. His strike across goal from a tight angle beat Scott Bain, but not the far post.

Haissem Hassan’s curler from the follow-up was then brilliantly tipped round the post by the keeper.

Jacob Murrell is the country’s in-form striker with five goals in his last seven outings, but sclaffed a shot wide from the penalty spot at the end of a lovely move involving Owen Eames and Scott Tanser down at the corner flag.

Duran should have levelled things up on the half-hour mark after getting on the end of a wicked Hassan ball into the six-yard box, but headed straight at Bain. Anywhere else but right down the middle would have done the trick.

He was made to pay for that miss as Falkirk doubled their advantage with a wonderful team goal on 38 minutes. Eames was given far too much space on the Falkirk left, but take nothing away from the way he threaded an inch-perfect pass into the path of the underlapping Tanser.

He took one touch to set himself as he drove into the box before coolly slotting past Johnstone. It was the kind of football we’ve become accustomed to seeing on a weekly basis from this side under John McGlynn.

Yes, Celtic looked like they couldn’t even be bothered to try and stop them but that’s not Falkirk’s problem. Their execution was flawless.

Man-of-the-Match Bain was once again called into action as the break came into view, and he once again stepped up, tipping Duran’s left-footed strike from 18 yards around the post.

Martin O'Neill looks on in dismay as Celtic suffer in Falkirk

O’Neill could have taken off any one of his so-called big-name stars at half-time and there would have been no grounds for complaint. He settled for just the one, replacing Callum Osmand with James Forrest.

Osmand should never be playing on the wing anyway. In Yang Hyun-Jun’s absence – and with Jota still searching for fitness – he has had a run of games in that position. You suspect he won’t be holding on to it for long. Square pegs in round holes, and all that.

If O’Neill did give his players a boot up the backside at the interval, you wouldn’t have known it, conceding a shocking third through Murrell within minutes of the restart. Fortunately for the visitors, they got away with it, with VAR spotting that the ball was bundled in by the striker’s hand.

Forrest forced a comfortable stop from Bain on the half-turn, with Callum McGregor then blazing over from a promising position.

The captain has been a shadow of himself all season. In truth, he looks a yard or two off the pace.

For so long, we’ve heard that Celtic just can’t do without him. However, playing like this, he isn’t helping this team.

Bain’s stop to deny Forrest on 68 minutes was simple enough. The one which denied substitute Benjamin Nygren seconds later to seal the points was right out of the top drawer.

The Bairns hadn’t beaten Celtic in 19 years coming into this one. Given the state of this Celtic side, is anyone truly surprised that run has come to a halt?

#1693. Report: Surprise €10m deal tabled for Liverpool veteran

Liverpool have a lot of decisions that they need to make on their squad over the next few months.

A handful of their first-team squad all have their contracts expiring in June 2027 and, with no negotiations lined up for any of them, another massive overhaul could be just around the corner.

Of course, the number of transfers that Liverpool have been linked with is obscene but, at least it proves that the Reds are casting their net far and wide for their next transfers.

Some positions are obviously more in need of reinforcement than others but, since Liverpool could end up moving some of their own players on as well, nobody actually knows what the next year or so could look like for the Anfield outfit.

That is, especially when multi-million deals are put up for grabs.

AC Milan want to offer Virgil van Dijk €10 million per year to join them from Liverpool

Virgil van Dijk has easily been one of Liverpool's best players ever since he joined.

No matter who he's been partnered with or who the Reds have faced, the Dutchman has always managed to come out as one of the stand-out performers.

Indeed, things have gone a bit wrong for him every now and then but, more often than not, he's proven why he's one of the world's best centre-backs.

However, now that he's 35 years old, questions are being asked about how long he can keep these performance levels up for.

Liverpool have already started to line up players such as Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet to replace him but, right now, Andoni Iraola's men would be lost without their captain in the starting XI.

So, that's why the latest update from MilanNews24 is so surprising.

"According to what MilanNews24 has learned, Cardinale would like to make a concrete attempt," they wrote.

"It's not just a tempting idea or a name linked to AC Milan to fuel the fans' ambitions: the Rossoneri owner is reportedly willing to seriously evaluate the conditions for bringing the Dutchman to Italy.

"To land Van Dijk, there are two key conditions. The first concerns Champions League qualification , a crucial element in presenting the defender with an ambitious and competitive sporting project.

"The second is naturally economic: a two-year contract worth 8-10 million euros per season would be on the table .

"A significant figure, which testifies to the scope of the investment envisioned by Cardinale.

"AC Milan is therefore dreaming of an international signing for the summer of 2027. Van Dijk would be a signing capable of bringing experience, leadership, and personality. Now they need to turn that dream into a concrete possibility."

Virgil van Dijk is still one of Liverpool's most important players

As mentioned, Van Dijk is key to the way that Liverpool play at the moment.

When he's left on the bench for a cup tie or a less important game, the difference in quality is staggering.

The Dutchman may not seem like he does all that much when he's on the pitch but, in reality, he's the glue that holds the team together.

Of course, other players such as Ronald Araujo or Joe Gomez can try and plug the gap left by the Dutchman but, neither of them are anywhere near his level.

It was always going to be a worry that Van Dijk would leave for free at the end of this season but, the fact that a concrete bid is about to come from AC Milan is surprising.

Most reports that emerge from Italy make it clear that most Serie A clubs are skint with several outfits often linked with haggling Liverpool for a discount on Federico Chiesa's impending transfer.

So, the fact that AC Milan are willing to give Van Dijk around €10 million per year is shocking.

His stature and name in the game will obviously carry a lot of weight but, unless you're a team who knows you can afford his wages such as Liverpool, it feels a tad strange for him to be targeted by anyone else.
